packages.docs:
Host-mediated action bus for Spores.

A Spore sees a granted action catalog and emits bounded invocations. The host
owns grants, approval, idempotency, credentials, routing, retries and audit.
Unibus adapters implement the actions; Spores never import Unibus or open a
connector-specific transport.

interfaces.docs:
Presentation projection of the granted action catalog.

This never grants execution. A caller may render a button or parameter form
from this data, then invoke through `actions.invoke`.
interfaces.name: catalog

packages.name: actions

packages.docs:
Host-attested context for an incoming HTTP invocation.

The host owns the listener, TLS, and routing. A Spore sees the request only
through `wasi:http`; this interface adds the host-side facts that must not be
spoofable request headers: which Spore ran, which route grant matched, and
who is on the other end of the transport.

`current` is valid only for the duration of one `incoming-handler` call. A
host that calls a component outside an HTTP invocation has no context to
report and fails the call rather than inventing one.
packages.name: http-context

packages.docs:
Mycelium control-plane capabilities exposed to Spores.

This is not the host directory/session surface in `soil:mycelium`. This
package is for daemon-owned control-plane state: schedules, runs and the
system tasks that share the same clock. The host bridges it to myceliumd;
the Spore never sees a socket, a store path or a node key.

functions.docs: System and user pulses. System entries are read-only.
functions.name: all

functions.docs:
Create or replace a user pulse. The host validates the cron expression
and the command before persisting it.
functions.name: put

functions.docs: Remove a user pulse by id.
functions.name: remove

functions.docs: Run history, newest first. `id` filters to one user pulse.
functions.name: runs

packages.name: mycelium

packages.docs:
Host world for the terminal Spore.

The host lives in Soil (`crates/terminal-host`); the Spore and its package
live in mycelium-linux/spores. Keeping the world beside the interfaces means
the host and the Spore cannot drift on a hand-copied dependency.
packages.name: terminal-spore

packages.docs:
Hook administration: the one door the CLI and a console both use.

This is a product contract, not a runtime one (`fungos:`, not `soil:`): only a
webhook product knows what a slug, a provider and a tenant are. The host
implements it because the host owns the registry and, later, Geode - a guest
that can create a hook is not a guest that should be able to read the secret
bytes behind one.

The secret crosses this boundary exactly once, in `created`. There is no
read, no export and no list-of-secrets: a hook that is lost is revoked and
made again, which is cheaper than a capability that hands out credentials.

functions.docs:
Register a hook and mint its credential.

One call, not two: a hook without a credential accepts nothing, and a
credential without a hook is a secret nobody owns.
functions.name: create

functions.docs: Every hook the caller may see. Never includes secrets.
functions.name: hooks

functions.docs:
Revoke a hook and its credential. `false` means it was already gone,
which is not an error - the caller wanted it absent and it is absent.
functions.name: revoke

types.docs: The only value that ever carries a secret.
types.name: created

types.docs: A registered endpoint. The secret is deliberately absent.
types.name: hook

packages.name: webhooks

packages.docs:
Observe and answer software agents, whatever harness runs them.

The subject is the set: every agent this surface may see, for one principal
or for a shared desktop. One control plane, one record per agent -- what it
is doing, what it needs from a person, and the few things a person may do.

An adapter is a host concern (Operator, Pi, another harness): it translates
native session events into these records and answers back. A Spore sees
facts, never a harness protocol, a credential, a process handle or a path.

The contract carries facts, not moods. Anything a view derives from them
(a creature's energy, a wall's ordering, a pulse's colour) belongs to the
view, so two views of the same agent cannot disagree about a fact the way two
copies of a derived field would.

interfaces.docs:
Control: the three things a person may do to an agent.

Deliberately not a general RPC to the harness. Starting sessions, editing
configuration, and choosing models are separate authorities with separate
grants; a surface that answers questions cannot also spawn processes.

functions.docs:
Ask the agent to stop the current turn. The agent stays observable and may
be sent another message afterwards.
functions.name: interrupt

functions.docs:
Answer one prompt. The prompt id makes this idempotent: answering a prompt
the agent already resolved is `stale`, not a second action.
functions.name: respond

functions.docs:
Say something to the agent as the user. Refused with `invalid` while a
prompt is open: an answer is not a message, and treating it as one is how
two people answer the same question twice.
functions.name: send

interfaces.name: control

interfaces.docs: Read-only: what the agents are doing.

functions.docs:
The agents this host can see, in the host's own order: agents that need a
person first, then most recently active. A view may reorder; a surface
that only has room for one row should not have to.
functions.name: agents

functions.docs:
What this surface is allowed to see. A wall over a shared desktop names
the desktop; a session window names the principal it was opened for.
(`current-scope` rather than `scope`: WIT keeps a function and a type in
one interface apart by name, and the record is the useful half to keep.)
functions.name: current-scope

functions.docs:
The devices this surface may place work on, in the host's own order.

Empty when the host was given no device: an adapter that has not thought
about placement offers no choice rather than one silent default. A surface
with no devices leaves its picker out; it does not invent a name.
functions.name: devices

functions.docs: The launch intent the host chose for this surface.
functions.name: intent

functions.docs:
The models the harnesses will accept, in the host's order.

Only strings a harness advertised: a picker that offered a name nobody
serves would be asking a person to choose a failure. Empty when no
harness named any, and then the picker is left out.
functions.name: models

functions.docs:
One subscription per surface. Changes that happened before it opened are
not replayed: `agents` is the snapshot, the subscription is the delta.
functions.name: subscribe

functions.docs:
Conversation text, newest page first. `limit` is bounded by the host; a
Spore asks again with `before` while the person scrolls back.
functions.name: transcript

interfaces.name: observe

types.docs:
One thing that happened, at one station.

`label` is a name, never content: a tool name, a harness step, two path
segments, a host. Folding neighbouring repeats into one row is a view
decision; the host reports what happened.
types.name: activity

types.docs:
The station vocabulary of an agent's timeline.

Fixed here so that every harness and every view agree on what a lit Files
station means. The adapter classifies; the view only draws. `other` is for
work that fits no station, and takes its label from the harness.
types.name: activity-kind

types.docs:
What the host opened this surface for.

A window dedicated to one agent gets its id; a wall that shows everything
gets none. `view` is a hint the Spore may ignore: views are the Spore's
vocabulary, not the contract's.
types.name: binding

types.docs:
One machine a person may place work on.

Facts, not capacity: `attached` says this host reached that device's agent
service when it opened the surface, and `detail` is why it did not. Nothing
here claims what the device could do later, and no field is a credential.
types.name: device

types.docs:
Who an agent belongs to.

A projection, not an identity: an agent on a shared desktop may belong to
a person this host cannot attest, and a fabricated `soil:principal`
identity would be worse than an honest label. `actor` is stable and
comparable; `display-name` is for people.
types.name: owner

types.docs:
Where an agent is in its turn.

`needs-you` is the only phase that implies a non-empty `prompts` list, and
a non-empty `prompts` list always implies `needs-you`. An adapter that
cannot represent an approval natively still satisfies the invariant: it
synthesizes a prompt (for example from a terminal `blocked` report) and
resolves it when the answer reaches the harness by whatever channel that
harness has.
types.name: phase

types.docs:
One thing the agent cannot decide alone.

A prompt is the only way an agent asks for a person. Everything that needs
a decision -- a permission request, a choice between approaches, a
terminal `blocked` report -- is normalized here, so a surface renders one
card shape instead of one per harness.
types.name: prompt

types.docs:
Whose agents a surface is showing.

Chosen by the host, never by the Spore: a surface bound to one principal
and a wall over a shared desktop are different authorities, and the grant
is what decides which one a caller gets.
types.name: scope-kind

packages.name: agents

packages.docs:
Private app storage.

AppData is scoped to the signed Spore's app identity and the current user.
The Spore sees opaque keys and bytes, never a host path, table, app id, or
another app's namespace.

`local` is device-only. `synced` is a per-app, per-user private book that
replicates through the native records engine. Synced AppData is not indexed
or shareable; structured/shareable data belongs in `soil:records`.

functions.docs: List metadata for keys under a prefix. Values are fetched separately.
functions.name: [method]store.list-keys

functions.docs: Last-writer-wins per key. Returns the new generation.
functions.name: [method]store.set

functions.docs: Compare-and-set against the caller's last observed generation.
functions.name: [method]store.set-if-generation

packages.name: appdata

packages.docs:
Host BLE radio capability.

Transport stays in Soil; the device protocol stays in the Spore. A Spore
receives Soil-issued device handles and characteristic UUIDs, never a MAC,
path, socket, permission, or radio handle it can forge.

A Spore may hold several links at once — two rings, a watch, a necklace — so
every link-scoped call names the link it applies to. Each link owns its own
event queue: a device that streams audio cannot starve a quiet one's
notifications.

Limits (Soil-enforced, not expressible in WIT):
- at most 64 devices per scan, 8 subscribed characteristics per link
- at most `max-links` concurrent links; further links fail `over-budget`
- a claimed device keeps its id in the host's session until re-claimed
- one live radio lease per device, held by one host at a time
- scan <= 30 s; next-event bounded per call; every call has a deadline
- read <= 512 B per call; write <= 512 B per call; the Spore chunks frames
- no fs, net, clock, env, or device enumeration beyond scan results

functions.docs:
Bind a scan handle to a caller-chosen id, once. Soil records the
peripheral's platform address in its session, so later scans report that
`device-id` before any read. This is how two identical devices with no
serial stay distinguishable: the wearer claims each one while it is the
only candidate, and identity is stable from then on. Re-claiming moves
the id to the current peripheral; `invalid` for an empty id.
functions.name: claim

functions.docs:
Connect to a previously scanned handle, returning a link handle. The host
takes that device's radio lease. Reconnecting to a device already linked
returns the existing link; when the budget is spent the call fails
`over-budget` before any handshake starts.
functions.name: connect

functions.docs:
Concurrent links this host will grant. Callers that need several devices
plan against this instead of discovering the ceiling by failing.
functions.name: max-links

functions.docs:
Wait up to `timeout-ms` for one event from that link's own queue; `none`
means the deadline expired and is not an error.
functions.name: next-event

functions.docs: Read at most `max-bytes` from a characteristic. `0` is `invalid`.
functions.name: read

functions.docs: Active scan for `timeout-ms`, returning Soil-issued handles.
functions.name: scan

functions.docs: Discovered GATT tree on that link.
functions.name: services

functions.docs:
Enable notifications for a characteristic on that link. Events are
drained with `next-event` for the same link.
functions.name: subscribe

types.docs:
Soil-issued handle for a scan result. Opaque; not an address. Valid only
until the next scan.
types.name: device-handle

types.docs: One inbound radio event.
types.name: event

types.docs:
Soil-issued handle for one live link. Opaque; not an address and not a
radio handle. Stale handles fail `not-connected`; they are never reused
within a Spore run.
types.name: link

types.docs:
One inbound notification. The UUID lets a Spore tell the command channel
from DFU; the payload is still opaque.
types.name: notification

packages.name: ble

packages.docs:
Canvas is the cross-platform owner: window, compositor, layout, theme,
rendering and input lifecycle stay in the host. A Spore is logic/data and
asks the granted Canvas surface to present or to receive normalized input.

Limits (host-enforced):
- one granted surface per Spore; the host selects extent and display
- one present and one input per invocation; no per-frame callback
- input is a bounded semantic key or one printable Unicode scalar, never a
  raw keycode, scan code or device event
- no pixels, framebuffer, DRM handle, window handle, path or clock

functions.docs: Release the grant. Further calls return `closed`.
functions.name: close

functions.docs:
Deliver one normalized event. `generation` must match the state the
caller last observed; a stale generation is refused, never reordered.
Text arrives as `character`; raw keycodes and platform scan codes never
cross this boundary.
functions.name: input

functions.docs: Read the current owner state without presenting.
functions.name: observe

functions.docs:
Present into the space the host granted.

`document` is a versioned payload from `soil-scene`: a scene the host
rasterizes, an RGBA frame the Spore rendered, or a lease on a GPU texture.
It is bytes rather than a WIT type on purpose -- a new node kind must not
rebuild every Spore that draws. The host validates it and refuses anything
it cannot present, naming the reason.
functions.name: present

types.docs:
Theme tokens the host has already resolved. A Spore-owned renderer reads
these instead of guessing colors from a screenshot or hard-coding its own.
types.name: theme

packages.name: canvas

packages.docs:
Host-owned audio codec sessions.

A Spore names a session and bounded packet/PCM bytes. The host owns libopus,
sample rates, channel layouts, codec state and resource limits; no guest sees
a decoder handle, native pointer, or codec configuration.

functions.docs: Decode one encoded packet for a session into interleaved PCM16.
functions.name: decode

functions.docs: Encode one interleaved PCM16 frame for a session.
functions.name: encode

functions.docs: Drop all codec state for a session.
functions.name: reset

packages.name: codec

packages.docs:
Host-mediated credentials.

A Spore names a credential and asks the host to sign or verify. Secret bytes
never enter the guest: `resolve` returns an opaque handle, and every
operation is re-checked against the host's grant and expiry on use.

The host adapter for this interface is Geode (Mycelium). This contract is
deliberately smaller than a key store: no enumeration, no read, no export.

functions.docs: Resolve a granted credential name to an opaque handle.
functions.name: resolve

functions.docs: Sign a message with a resolved handle.
functions.name: sign

functions.docs:
Sign with a PGP key. Kept separate from `algorithm` so a guest built
against the two-variant enum keeps its ABI when PGP is added.
functions.name: sign-pgp

functions.docs:
Verify a signature with a resolved handle. A mismatched signature is
`ok(false)`, not an error; errors describe the credential or request.
functions.name: verify

functions.docs: Verify a detached PGP signature.
functions.name: verify-pgp

packages.name: creds

packages.docs:
Which Desktops this machine offers, and which one a window is operating on.

A Desktop is a durable namespace a Spore browses. It is not a host folder:
the Spore learns identity, presentation and access, never a path. That is the
whole surface. `available` says what exists; `open` moves this window, which is why
there is no `root` or `mount` anywhere in these types — a caller that could
name a path could read a Desktop it was never granted.

A window is bound to exactly one Desktop. Rebinding is a barrier, not a
setting: quiesce, swap the workspace, invalidate the cached listing, reset the
path and selection to the new root. View mode and sort order survive, because
losing them on every switch makes the picker expensive to use. A refusal
(`denied`) leaves the window on the Desktop it was already on.

"All desktops" is a read-only scope for search, not a workspace: it has no
root and `open` refuses it. Hits from that scope are tagged with the Desktop
they came from, so a result never has to be guessed back to its home.

functions.docs:
Every Desktop this machine registers, with this window's access to each.

Named `available`, not `list`: `list` is a WIT keyword and cannot name a
function. It reads the same way — *what is available to this window*.

Rows the principal cannot open are listed rather than hidden: a picker that
silently omits a Desktop reads as "it does not exist", which is a different
and much worse claim than "you cannot open this".
functions.name: available

functions.docs:
Bind this window to `id` and return it as the window now sees it.

Callable while already bound, including for the Desktop it is bound to.
functions.name: open

types.docs: How far this window may go in one Desktop.
types.name: access

packages.name: desktops

packages.docs:
Semantic device capabilities.

Runtime uses the documented bounded core-Wasm lowering, not component
canonical ABI. Battery is measured, estimate is model output, and lid is a
read-only switch observation. Grants remain per interface.

interfaces.docs:
Semantic interface. Runtime uses the documented core-Wasm lowering, not
component canonical ABI. Tokens are invocation-scoped, single-use handles.
interfaces.name: battery

interfaces.docs:
Model output, never measured SOC or kernel battery capacity. Runtime uses
the documented bounded core-Wasm lowering, not component canonical ABI.
interfaces.name: estimate

interfaces.docs:
Read-only lid capability. Host grants permission per guest; never grants
raw device access, socket selection, display policy or input injection.

functions.docs:
Bounded diagnostic: guest requests logging its most recent read.
Not arbitrary text and not device/display authority.
functions.name: log-change

interfaces.name: lid

packages.name: device

packages.docs:
Git status for the repository a workspace path is inside.

A Spore cannot run git, and it must not learn where this machine keeps a
checkout. It names a canonical workspace-relative path and receives what the
repository says about itself: a branch, a commit, and counts. No host path,
no remote URL, no commit message crosses the boundary.

Status is read when it is asked for, never cached: a branch that changed a
second ago would otherwise be reported with yesterday's name.

functions.docs: Status of the repository containing `path`.
functions.name: status

packages.name: git

packages.docs:
Read-only graph queries over explicit record links and references.

The graph is derived from records in host-approved books. A node or edge is
a locator; this contract never grants access to the target.

functions.docs: Query edges attached to `node`. Empty `rel` means every relationship.
functions.name: neighbors

functions.docs: Query external identifiers attached to `node`.
functions.name: references

packages.name: graph

packages.docs:
Bounded host-mediated HTTP.

The guest names an absolute URL and an optional host-resolved credential
handle. The host checks its origin allowlist, injects the credential, refuses
unbounded bodies and redirects, and returns one bounded response. Raw sockets,
DNS control, proxy configuration and secret bytes never cross this boundary.
packages.name: http

packages.docs:
Derived, rebuildable index over the VFS namespace.

The index is not authority. It never creates, mutates or owns a file; it
answers browse/search queries and returns paths. The Spore then calls
`soil:vfs.stat`/`read` for the authoritative entry and bytes. A host may
rebuild the index at any time and bump `generation`.

functions.docs: Browse direct children in the requested order.
functions.name: browse

functions.docs:
Exact KNN over the host embedding index. Returns `unsupported` when the
host has no embedding provider; guests never choose a model.
functions.name: knn

functions.docs:
Rebuild from the current VFS namespace. Hosts may also rebuild in the
background; this call is the explicit refresh boundary.
functions.name: refresh

functions.docs:
Search paths, media types, metadata, and indexed text. Results are paths;
call `soil:vfs.stat` for authoritative entry data.
functions.name: search

functions.docs: Inspect index readiness and generation.
functions.name: state

packages.name: index

packages.docs:
Host-mediated language-model inference.

The host owns provider selection, endpoint discovery, authentication, model
aliases, budgets, and transport. A Spore names a model, messages, and tools.
Credentials and provider routes never cross this boundary.

functions.docs: Read the next chunk. `none` means the timeout elapsed without data.
functions.name: [method]completion-stream.next

functions.docs: Non-streaming completion.
functions.name: complete

functions.docs:
Non-streaming text embeddings. The host scrubs every input before it
leaves the process and returns vectors in input order.
functions.name: embed

functions.docs: List models visible to this host/profile.
functions.name: models

functions.docs:
Open a streaming completion. The returned resource is bounded by the host
session and must be cancelled or dropped when the guest is done.
functions.name: open-stream

functions.docs:
Non-streaming speech-to-text. PCM16 goes to the host's STT route, never to
the chat route. Segments and words stay in provider order.
functions.name: transcribe

functions.docs:
Non-streaming speaker embedding. This is an audio path, deliberately
separate from text `embed`: it sends PCM16, not scrubbed text.
functions.name: voice-embed

types.docs:
What a model can do. A host fills these from its provider catalog; a
guest uses them to pick a tier without hardcoding provider names.
types.name: capability

types.docs: Streaming response handle. The guest polls it at its own cadence.
types.name: completion-stream

types.docs:
One PCM16LE mono utterance or window for transcription. The host owns the
STT route and model; the guest only names the audio and optional language.
types.name: transcribe-request

types.docs:
One PCM16LE mono utterance for speaker/voice embedding. The model and
checkpoint are named explicitly: voice templates are only comparable to
embeddings from the same pipeline.
types.name: voice-embedding-request

packages.name: inference

packages.docs:
Shared normalized input types.

Presentation surfaces (Canvas, Terminal, imported surfaces) use the same
semantic key, pointer, scroll and text vocabulary. The host owns platform
keycode and IME translation; guests only see these normalized values.

types.docs:
Host-normalized key. `named` is an escape hatch for imported native
surfaces that expose stable semantic names the host cannot map further.
types.name: key

types.docs: Normalized surface coordinates, 0..=1.
types.name: point

packages.name: input

packages.docs:
Host-mediated media sources.

A Spore names a host-reviewed source id. It never receives a URL, Unibus
peer, API token, decoder handle, or raw socket. Playback is decoded and
presented by the host; encoded access is a separate grant.

types.docs:
Explicit encoded access for recording, remuxing, transcoding, inspection,
or a codec the host cannot present. Not implied by playback.
types.name: encoded-stream

types.docs:
One decoded image. The host may downsample to satisfy the requested
bounds; the returned dimensions are authoritative.
types.name: image

types.docs:
Host-owned playback. The host owns demuxing, decode, A/V clock, audio
device, and presentation surface.
types.name: playback

packages.name: media

packages.docs:
Publish metrics from a Spore, scrape them from the host.

A Spore cannot open a socket, and a metric is not an action: it is a fact
about the work the Spore already did. This is the narrowest surface for that
fact — a Spore names a series and a value, the host keeps the registry, and
the host's HTTP surface answers `GET /metrics` in Prometheus text format.

The host is the one that exposes it, so a Spore never learns a port, a path,
or a scraper. Each Spore has its own registry and the host renders it on that
Spore's vhost, so one Spore's series can never be attributed to another; a
series with two kinds under one name is refused rather than rendered twice.

Alerting is not here. A scrape is a sample; an alert is a decision with a
person on the other end, and those travel as `soil:unibus` frames (the
`fpl.node.health.v1` shape the fleet feed already consumes). Keeping them
apart is what lets a dashboard and an alert disagree only about thresholds,
never about the numbers.

functions.docs: Record samples. Counters add to the series; gauges replace it.
functions.name: emit

functions.docs:
What the registry currently holds, for a Spore that renders its own view
and for tests. The HTTP surface is the host's, not the Spore's.
functions.name: snapshot

packages.name: metrics

packages.docs:
Mycelium-backed directory and terminal session capability.

The host owns identity, certificates, routing, jump hosts, host-key
verification and the SSH profile. A Spore names an opaque target id obtained
from `directory`; it never supplies a host, port, credential or private key.

The handles below are component-instance-scoped and unforgeable in the sense
that the host only accepts handles it issued. A later revision can replace
them with WIT resources without changing the verbs.

functions.docs: Fetch one visible target without listing.
functions.name: get

functions.docs: List visible targets. `kind` is a display filter, not authority.
functions.name: targets

functions.docs: Run a non-interactive command for agents. No PTY, no VT semantics.
functions.name: exec

functions.docs:
Open an interactive PTY shell through the host's Mycelium SSH profile.
`cols` and `rows` seed the remote terminal size.
functions.name: open-shell

functions.docs:
Read bytes from the PTY. Empty list means the timeout elapsed; `none`
means the session reached EOF.
functions.name: read

functions.docs: Tell the remote PTY its new window size.
functions.name: resize

functions.docs: Write input bytes to the PTY.
functions.name: write

packages.name: mycelium

packages.docs:
Bounded host-mediated name resolution and TCP reachability.

The guest names a host or a mesh node (`<node>.<site>.myc`), never a socket,
resolver address, or packet. The host resolves through its own resolver (the
mesh one for `.myc`), bounds every lookup and connect by the caller's
deadline, and returns data. Raw ICMP, arbitrary ports sweeps and resolver
configuration never cross this boundary.

functions.docs: Resolve, then connect and close a TCP session to prove the service is up.
functions.name: probe

functions.docs: Resolve a name. `<node>.<site>.myc` is answered by the mesh resolver.
functions.name: resolve

packages.name: net

packages.docs:
Host-mediated notifications, focus, history and cleanup.

A publisher emits a durable notification envelope. An inbox shows and acts on
it. Focus is a host-owned per-device policy; history is opt-in and separately
granted. No payload carries app identity, a URL, a credential or authority.
packages.name: notify

packages.docs:
How a Spore hands over what it rendered.

One interface, two deliveries. A Spore either hands over the pixels it
rasterized (`rgba`) or the texture it rendered (`texture`); the host turns
whichever it receives into the next frame. The extent is always the host's:
`size()` is the only authority, so a Spore cannot choose or resize a display.

Both deliveries are bytes-free of documents on purpose: no scene graph, no
JSON, no per-frame schema negotiation. A frame is an extent and a buffer, or
a texture handle.

This interface is bound two ways, and that is an implementation detail of the
host, not a second contract:

* a component host binds it directly through the canonical ABI
  (`soil-webgpu`, `canvas-winit`);
* a core-Wasm host lowers the same functions by hand
  (`soil-runtime`, see `docs/abi-core-wasm.md`).

A Spore targets `surface` once and runs against either.

interfaces.docs:
The system clipboard. A Spore selects text; the presenter owns the
pasteboard, so selection stays a Spore concern and the transfer is one call.
interfaces.name: clipboard

interfaces.docs:
Cursor shape for the window. The Spore says what it is pointing at; the
presenter applies it. A headless or capture host reports success and does
nothing, so no Spore has to test which host it is running under.
interfaces.name: cursor

interfaces.docs:
Keyboard and pointer events from the presenter. The Spore decides what they
mean; the host only normalizes them. Keys and pointer actions share one
ordered stream, so a click that lands between two keystrokes cannot be
reordered against them.

functions.docs:
True when a live presenter is attached and the guest should keep polling.
A one-shot capture host returns false and the guest exits after one frame.
functions.name: interactive

functions.docs: Wait up to `timeout-ms` for the next event. Zero polls without waiting.
functions.name: poll

interfaces.name: input

types.docs:
Pointer position in the presenter's surface space: the same units
`soil:present/surface.size` reports, origin top-left. A Spore that lays out
against that size hit-tests with these numbers directly, at any device
pixel ratio, without converting between logical and physical pixels itself.
types.name: pointer-move

types.docs:
Wheel movement in notches. Positive `lines` scrolls towards earlier
content (the wheel rolled away from the user); a host that only has pixel
deltas converts them to whole notches before queueing.
types.name: pointer-scroll

interfaces.docs:
The surface a Spore presents into. The host owns the window, the z-order and
the display; the Spore owns its layout and its rasterizer.

functions.docs:
Which deliveries this host accepts. A host with no GPU says `rgba` only,
which is what lets a Spore run on a device without a graphics stack.
functions.name: delivery

functions.docs: Copy one guest-rendered texture into the compositor's next frame.
functions.name: present

functions.docs:
Copy one guest-rendered RGBA8 frame into the compositor's next frame.

This is the arm for a Spore with its own rasterizer -- Slint's software
renderer, egui, Skia -- which needs no GPU, no `wasi:webgpu` and no
texture readback. The host validates extent and opacity, then presents it
in the space it granted.
functions.name: present-rgba

functions.docs:
Device pixels per layout pixel. A Spore that renders its own texture asks
before it opens a framebuffer, so the frame it presents is at the
resolution the window will actually blit rather than a fixed guess.
functions.name: scale

functions.docs:
The surface extent in the Spore's layout space. A Spore lays out against
these numbers and the presenter blits whatever resolution it renders at,
so the same layout matches the window on any display scale.
functions.name: size

interfaces.name: surface

types.docs:
Which deliveries the host can accept. A Spore asks once and picks the
renderer it already has, instead of inferring from a failed call.
types.name: delivery-kind

types.docs:
Tightly packed RGBA8, `width * height * 4` bytes, alpha 255.

The extent is the host's: it equals `size()`, never a size the Spore
chose. A frame that disagrees with it is refused, not resampled.
types.name: rgba-frame

packages.name: present

packages.docs:
Host-attested principal identity.

Mycelium identity / OIDC is the source of truth. The host verifies the
token or device identity and exposes only this minimal projection. Tokens,
refresh credentials, raw claims and private keys never cross the boundary.

A principal answers "who". It does not grant access; exact WIT grants and
book grants still decide what the caller may do and where.

functions.docs: Present only when this principal has a host-managed signing key.
functions.name: signing-key

types.docs:
Non-secret projection of the key this principal signs with.

The host owns the key through Geode or an enclave. This record never
carries private material; it is what a verifier or a store needs to name
the signer and resolve its public key.
types.name: signing-key-info

packages.name: principal

packages.docs:
Durable, schema-tagged records with a change feed and peer sync.

Records are the storage layer for Spores that need queryable state (mail and
chat metadata, contacts, CRM snapshots) without inventing a second database.
The host owns durability, revisions, tombstones, and sync. A Spore owns the
schema and the meaning of `body`.

Grants are separate: read, write, and sync. A read-only Spore cannot mutate
or export the store.

functions.docs:
Merge remote changes with last-writer-wins. This never calls back into
the network; the Spore or host transports the page.
functions.name: apply

functions.docs:
Export changes after `since`, ordered by `(revision, origin)`. This is the
sync producer side; pass the result to `apply` on the peer.
functions.name: changes

functions.docs:
Conditional create/replace/delete.

`expected = none` means create only if there is no live record.
`expected = some(version)` requires the current live record to match
exactly. On a mismatch the host returns `applied = false` and the
current entry; it never overwrites the winner. A missing record with an
expected version returns `not-found`.
functions.name: compare-and-swap

functions.docs:
Write a tombstone. The record remains visible to `changes` until the
host's tombstone retention expires.
functions.name: delete

functions.docs: Read one record.
functions.name: get

functions.docs:
Scan one collection in revision order. A cursor from a previous page is
valid until the host reports `stale`.
functions.name: scan

functions.docs:
Scan live records packed into one buffer. Same cursor and limit rules as
`scan`, but the entries are framed bytes rather than a list of records.
functions.name: scan-packed

functions.docs:
Create or replace a local record. The host assigns `revision` and
`origin`; the returned entry is authoritative.
functions.name: upsert

types.docs:
Result of a conditional write. On conflict `entry` is the current
authoritative entry, so the caller can re-read and retry.
types.name: cas-result

types.docs:
One stored record. `body` is opaque to the host (JSON, CBOR, or a Spore
schema); `schema` names the body contract.

Local `upsert` ignores `revision` and `origin` and assigns both. Remote
`apply` uses them for last-writer-wins:
  higher `revision` wins; equal revision is broken by lexicographic
  `origin`; a `deleted` entry is a tombstone.
types.name: entry

types.docs:
A record address. `collection` is a Spore-defined namespace
(`email.message`, `chat.message`, `contact`); `id` is stable within it.
types.name: key

types.docs:
A page of live records packed into one buffer.

The frame is, repeated until the buffer ends, all integers little-endian:
  u32 id-length, id bytes, u64 revision, u32 body-length, body bytes

This exists for callers that read a whole book: lowering thousands of
`entry` values costs more than the bytes, while one `list<u8>` crosses the
boundary once. There is no `deleted` field; packed scans are live-only.
types.name: packed-page

types.docs: The exact revision/origin tuple returned by a local write.
types.name: version

packages.name: records

packages.docs:
The scene payload is data, not an interface: it is what `soil:canvas.present`
carries, and it is versioned inside the document so a new node kind never
rebuilds the Spores that draw.

This package exists only so a Spore can ask the host what it accepts before it
builds a document. It deliberately does not describe the document's shape --
that lives in `soil-scene` (Rust) and is checked at present time, where a
producer can be told *why* something was refused.

functions.docs:
Host-enforced ceilings, so a producer can budget against the same numbers
the host will refuse at rather than discovering them by trial.
functions.name: budget

functions.docs:
Highest schema version the host can draw. A producer that needs newer
nodes gets `false` here instead of a failure at present time.
functions.name: supports

packages.name: scene

packages.docs:
Host-composed global search across granted local sources.

This is a derived discovery surface, not authority. Files still come from
`soil:vfs`, records from `soil:records`, and actions from their owning host
capability. A hit is a locator plus display metadata; the caller fetches the
authoritative object through the source capability.

interfaces.docs:
Typed mention resolver for `@` autocomplete.

A candidate is a stable locator, never a copied display name. The caller
inserts `token` into a document/task/record and persists it as a
`mentions` graph link. The host resolves labels and visibility from the
same approved books used by search.

functions.docs:
Resolve a prefix into typed candidates. Empty `kinds` means all supported
kinds. `limit` is host-bounded.
functions.name: suggest

interfaces.name: mentions

types.docs:
A typed graph reference attached to a hit. This is discovery metadata,
not an access grant or a fetched object.
types.name: reference

packages.name: search

packages.docs:
Installed Spore catalog and host-owned launch.

A Spore never scans the filesystem, starts a process, or chooses a window.
The host validates packages, maps them to a launch target, and performs the
launch outside the guest.

0.2.0 is a break, deliberately: `launch` answers with a `failure` (a code and
the host's own sentence) instead of a bare enum, and the catalogue gained
`running` and `stop`. A package built against 0.1.0 must fail as *too old* —
the host says which interface it speaks — rather than instantiate into an
arity mismatch that reads like a compiler bug in the window.

functions.docs:
Install `id` from the store this host is pointed at.

Installing is the host's act, not the window's: the guest names a listing,
and the host fetches, verifies, writes and compiles it. A host with no
store — a machine that is not pointed at one — answers `denied` rather than
pretending, and a package that arrives already installed is `installed`
again rather than a second copy.
functions.name: install

functions.docs:
Launch `surface` of `id`.

Fails with `unsupported` when this host cannot present the surface's kind
— a host without a browser view refuses a `web` surface rather than
opening something it cannot render. A name the package does not declare
is `not-found`. A package this host cannot start says so in `detail`.
functions.name: launch

functions.docs:
The ids this host started and has not seen exit, in catalogue order.

A launcher draws its running dot from this rather than from a pid file it
keeps itself: the host is what starts and reaps a Spore, so the host is
the only thing that knows whether one is still up.
functions.name: running

functions.docs:
Stop a Spore this host started.

`not-found` when nothing by that id is running. Stopping is the host's
act — the guest names the tile, the host ends the process.
functions.name: stop

types.docs:
Why a launch or a stop did not happen.

`code` is what a program branches on and `detail` is what a person reads:
the host knows which import it does not link, which file a package claims
but does not carry, or why a stop was refused, and none of that survives
an enum. The sentence is the host's, so the window never has to guess at
one — and a host with nothing to add sends an empty string.
types.name: failure

types.docs: What installing produced, so a window can say what changed.
types.name: installed

types.docs:
One view a package ships, declared so a host can tell what it would have
to provide before it opens anything.

`entry` is a path inside the package, never a content id. The package is
the unit of identity and provenance: its lock and digest already cover
every byte under its root, so a per-asset content id would be a second
version of the same fact and the two would drift.
types.name: surface

types.docs:
How a host presents a surface.

Native rendering is deliberately absent: it is the default, it is what
`[module]` and `[ui]` already are, and a package that needs nothing extra
should not have to declare it.
types.name: surface-kind

interfaces.docs:
Changing what opens by default.

Split from `open` so a surface that offers the picker does not thereby gain
the authority to change the default — the same read/write split as
`soil:agents`' observe and control.

functions.docs:
Drop the preference for one kind, so the default falls back to the most
specific candidate.
functions.name: clear

functions.docs:
`kind` is a media type or an extension glob. `id` must already be a
candidate for it: storing a preference for something that cannot open the
kind would be storing a lie.
functions.name: set

interfaces.name: defaults

interfaces.docs:
Host-owned package installation.

A Spore names a package by id and digest; it never names a path, a URL or a
grant. The host resolves the digest against its signed index, verifies the
tar, checks the import/grant rule, and only then swaps the install root.
Installing is the storefront's question, never its authority.

functions.name: install

functions.docs: Roll back to the one previous digest kept in `.packages`.
functions.name: rollback

functions.docs: What this host currently runs, if anything.
functions.name: status

interfaces.name: install

interfaces.docs:
Opening a document: which Spore can, and which one was asked for.

Two facts with different owners. What a Spore can open is its own `handles`
declaration in the manifest; what *should* open something is a preference,
and it lives in the desktop's `fungos/desktop/filetypes` book. A preference
may only choose among declarations — an id that no longer handles the kind is
skipped, never obeyed.

Not yet imported by either world: the shape is agreed, the host backend and
the guest bindings land next, and wiring an unbuilt interface into a world
would hand every Spore a function that refuses.

functions.docs: Everything installed that declares this path's kind, most specific first.
functions.name: candidates

functions.docs:
What this Spore was launched to open — the same job `soil:agents.intent()`
does for a surface. `none` for a Spore started any other way.
functions.name: intent

functions.docs:
Open it with the default. `no-default` when candidates exist but no
preference chose one, so the caller opens a picker instead of guessing.
functions.name: open

interfaces.name: open

types.docs: One Spore that can open the path.
types.name: candidate

types.docs:
Why an open could not happen. `no-candidates` and `no-default` are
different answers: the first says nothing installed can read this, the
second says something can but nobody has said which should.
types.name: error

types.docs:
What happened when a Spore opened something. Identity, not a process
handle: the caller learns what opened the document and gains no authority
over it.
types.name: launched

packages.name: spore

packages.docs:
Host content-addressed asset cache.

A Spore names a CID, never a path, directory, URL or handle. `read` is
granted by `soil:storage.read` (the default) and `write` by the separate
`soil:storage.write` grant. Writes reach a bounded host cache, never the
asset store or the Spore Store.

functions.docs:
Read the bytes named by a CIDv1 content address.

`max-bytes` bounds the response: an object larger than the limit is
`over-budget`, never a partial payload. `max-bytes == 0` is `invalid`.
functions.name: read

functions.docs:
Commit bytes to the bounded host cache under a CIDv1 address.

Requires `soil:storage.write`; without it the call is `denied`. The host
may refuse an oversized or over-capacity write with `over-budget`. This
never mutates the published asset store.
functions.name: write

packages.name: storage

packages.docs:
Host-issued byte streams.

A Spore never creates a listener, dials a socket, or holds a TLS key. The
host accepts the transport, authenticates the peer, and queues a bounded
duplex session. A Spore polls `accept`, then reads and writes the bytes.

functions.docs:
`none` is end of stream. A read never waits forever; the host may
return `none` when the peer is gone or the session was closed.
functions.name: [method]session.read

functions.docs:
Take the next authenticated session for `protocol`, or `none` when the
queue is empty. This is a poll, not a listener.
functions.name: accept

packages.name: streams

packages.docs:
Host-owned imported surfaces.

A surface is a native view, remote stream, decoded video, browser view, or
another Spore's render target. The host owns the pixels/texture and composes
them into Canvas. A Spore receives an opaque handle, metadata, damage, and
normalized input only.

types.docs:
Host-owned surface. The host may present, encode, or composite it; the
Spore never receives a texture or native window handle.
types.name: surface

packages.name: surface-import

interfaces.docs:
A live terminal screen: the host owns the PTY and the emulator (soil-vt),
the Spore renders the snapshot and sends keys back.

functions.docs:
Start another shell and make it the one `snapshot` and `write` act on.
`command` is a program line, or a login shell when absent.
functions.name: open-session
scroll

functions.docs: Point `snapshot`, `write`, `scroll`, `resize` and `wait` at a session.
functions.name: select-session

functions.docs: Every session the host is running, in the order the tabs should show them.
functions.name: sessions

functions.docs:
Block until the grid changes or the timeout expires, and answer the
generation that is current when it returns. A renderer waits on this
instead of polling, so a keystroke's echo is drawn the moment the
emulator publishes it rather than on the next tick.
functions.name: wait

interfaces.name: screen

types.docs:
One shell the host is running. A terminal shows them as tabs; the Spore
never owns a process, so the list comes from the host.
types.name: session

packages.docs:
Host-rendered terminal surface.

The Spore owns VT parsing (for example with libghostty-vt) and submits a
bounded cell grid. The host owns fonts, shaping, pixels, accessibility and
the input lifecycle. The host never receives raw escape sequences.

Handles are component-instance-scoped. A later revision can replace them
with WIT resources.

functions.docs: Wait for one normalized key or paste. `none` means the timeout elapsed.
functions.name: next-input

functions.docs: Submit a complete frame. Full-frame for v0; damage regions are additive.
functions.name: present

packages.name: terminal

packages.docs:
Host clocks: elapsed time and wall time.

Requires the `soil:time` grant. There is no sleep, timer thread or per-frame
callback: a Spore reads a clock and waits on a bounded tick. The host may
return a tick earlier than requested, so callers must re-check their deadline.

Two clocks, deliberately separate. Monotonic time answers "how long", wall
time answers "when". Mixing them is how a clock jumps an hour across a
daylight-saving boundary and a cache silently expires.

functions.docs:
Monotonic milliseconds from an unspecified host epoch.

Only useful for measuring elapsed time. Values are not comparable across
processes, host restarts or devices.
functions.name: monotonic-ms

functions.docs:
Wait up to `timeout-ms` for the next host tick and return its monotonic
millisecond value. `0` polls without blocking; `none` means the deadline
elapsed. A returned tick may precede the requested deadline.
functions.name: tick

functions.docs: The current wall-clock instant.
functions.name: wall-clock

types.docs:
One wall-clock instant, already resolved into local components.

The host owns the timezone: a Spore never converts from UTC, never guesses
an offset, and never reaches for a locale. Components are provided rather
than a formatted string so a view can lay out "14:32" and "Tue 14:32"
without parsing anything, and `offset-minutes` is included so a caller can
label the value without a second call.
types.name: date-time

packages.name: time

packages.docs:
Bounded observation and publication on the Unibus.

Unibus L1 routes opaque envelopes; this capability is the Spore-facing edge.
It never exposes credentials, peer identities, or raw sockets. A Spore
subscribes by kind and receives metadata/body bytes; it does not get bus
internals or the ability to bypass grants.

functions.docs:
Poll retained frames for the listed kinds. An empty `kinds` list means
no kinds, never "all"; a Spore must name what it observes.
functions.name: poll

functions.docs:
Publish one frame. Requires `soil:unibus.publish`; destinations and TTL
are bounded by the host. No credentials cross this boundary.
functions.name: publish

packages.name: unibus

packages.docs:
Content-addressed lookup inside the VFS namespace.

`soil:vfs` is addressed by path, because a namespace has paths. A record has
none: it is copied to peers that never saw this machine's workspace, and the
bytes it names may be here, on a peer, or nowhere yet. So a record names
identity (`blake3:<hex>`, the `content-id` `soil:vfs` already publishes), and
this interface answers the other question: where in *this* workspace do those
bytes live?

A content id is not authority. The answer is entries the caller could already
see by walking the namespace, never a host path, a provider locator, a URL or
a lease. A Spore that can read `soil:vfs` learns nothing new about the
machine by asking; a Spore that cannot is refused here as it is there.

Separate from `soil:vfs` on purpose, the way `soil:vfs-mut` is: a host opts in
to a new grant without re-versioning the interface every existing Spore
already imports, and a Spore that never resolves a content id never sees it.

functions.docs:
Entries whose whole-content identity is `content-id`, in path order.

Empty is a real answer: the bytes are not in this workspace. That is not a
deletion — deletion is a tombstone in `soil:records` — and a caller that
conflated the two would make a cache miss look like lost data.

Two paths holding the same bytes both answer. That is the point: the
identity is the bytes, not the name.
functions.name: find

packages.name: vfs-cid

packages.docs:
Bounded, explicitly granted VFS mutation.

This is a separate grant from read-only `soil:vfs`. Paths remain canonical
workspace-relative paths; the Spore never receives a host path, descriptor,
provider locator, or raw CID.

functions.docs:
Open a streaming writer. `expected-size` is an advisory quota; the host
may still enforce a smaller per-principal limit.
functions.name: begin-write

functions.docs:
Change permission bits without touching content. A mode belongs to the
entry, not to a version of the bytes, so this adds no version.
functions.name: chmod

functions.docs: Unlink a namespace entry. Content and history are retained.
functions.name: remove

functions.docs: Rename a file. Directory renames are not part of this slice.
functions.name: rename

functions.docs:
Create or replace one file. `expected-version` is the optimistic
concurrency check; `none` means create/replace unconditionally. `mode`
names the permission bits for a caller that has a real file to describe
(the overlay applying a build); `none` keeps the current mode, or `0o644`
for a path that did not exist.
functions.name: write

types.docs:
Stream one file into the VFS. The host owns the temp object, hashing,
quotas and the atomic commit. `write` returns the bytes accepted so far.
types.name: writer

packages.name: vfs-mut

packages.docs:
Read-only VFS namespace.

The Spore names a workspace-relative path, never a host filesystem path,
directory handle, descriptor, URL or CID supplied as authority. The host
canonicalizes the path, enforces the workspace boundary, and applies a
bounded page/range budget. Listing is deterministic by path; sort/search is
`soil:index`'s job.

`read` returns bytes for an already-present object or hydrates a placeholder
through the host's granted content transport. The Spore never chooses the
provider, endpoint, token or lease. A range larger than the host budget is
`over-budget`, never silently truncated.

functions.docs:
List direct children of `parent` in path order.
`parent` empty means the workspace root. `limit` is host-bounded.
functions.name: ls

functions.docs:
Read a bounded byte range. `length == 0` is `invalid`.
The host hydrates a placeholder if its transport grant allows it.
functions.name: read

functions.docs: Fetch one namespace entry without reading its bytes.
functions.name: stat

packages.name: vfs

packages.docs:
Host-owned web/Spore/retained view.

The target is an id in the host's reviewed index, never an arbitrary URL,
path or CID supplied by wasm. The host owns the browser/Spore engine, pixels
and capture buffer; the Spore owns presentation state and normalized actions.

functions.docs: PNG
functions.name: [method]view.close

packages.name: view

packages.docs:
The checkouts a Desktop knows, read as the rows `mush attach` records.

A project is a repository, not a directory: `project` is `owner/repo` (the
spelling GitHub and Operator use), and a checkout and the worktrees cut from
it share it. The host keeps the remote's host beside that identity as a dedupe
key; it is not part of the name, so a Spore never has to know it. The Desktop
owns the rows; this interface only reads them. Attaching and detaching stay
host commands, so a Spore cannot widen what a Desktop knows.

functions.docs: Every checkout this Desktop knows, in path order.
functions.name: checkouts

types.docs:
What a checkout is: the repository itself, a tree linked to one, or a path
the Desktop lists without being able to read git from it.
types.name: role

packages.name: worktrees

packages.docs:
Draft `wasi:audio` proposal, maintained in Soil while no upstream package
exists. This is a bounded PCM sink, not the WebAudio graph API.

functions.docs: Wait until the host queue is empty or the bounded timeout expires.
functions.name: [method]output.drain

functions.docs:
Push interleaved f32 frames. Returns the number of complete frames
accepted; zero means backpressure, not failure.
functions.name: [method]output.write
